pll1d39c2-d1e3501.summary: Reports the objection: if God can know or foreknow what he never knew, he can know something in time.

pll1d39c2-d1e3504.summary: Answers: God can know whatever he can do, and he can do what will never be, so he can know what never is, though he does not know it, since his knowledge is only of what is, was, or will be. But he cannot begin to know it; he can know it now as he could have from eternity. 'He can now know what he did not know from eternity,' if meaning both at once, is false; if meaning he has the power from eternity and now to know something that is not foreknown, it is true. So God cannot know or will anything newly, though he can will what he never willed.
claims: God can know what he can make but will not.
God cannot begin to know anything.

pl-l1d39c2.summary: Answers the objection that if God can know what he never knew, he can know something newly in time. God can know or foreknow whatever he can make, and he can make what will never be, so he can know what never is; but he cannot begin to know it. He can now know it only in the sense that he could have known it from eternity. 'He can now know what he did not know from eternity' is false if meaning both together, true if meaning he has the power from eternity and now to know something, though it is not known. So God cannot know or will anything newly, though he can will what he never willed.
claims: God can know whatever he can make, including what will never be.
God's knowledge concerns only what is, was, or will be; foreknowledge only the future.
God cannot know anything newly or in time.
God can now know something only as he could have known it from eternity.
Likewise God cannot will anything newly, though he can will what he never willed.
